feedback: Before this robot races: iteration 2 (row ±0.02 at 12 mm, y=0.04, kp 1.0, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.1) scored 63.85, up from 57.11. Slalom oscillation fell from 0.150 to 0.145, and progress rose on the oval (0.176) and s-bend (0.189). Max error still reached about 0.06 m on every run, so the off-track limit is the binding failure. The 12 mm row at ±0.02 covers offsets only to about 0.0385 m. Your widened row at ±0.03 with 16 mm sensors extends that to about 0.0505 m, which is the right direction for the line loss seen after progress 0.1. I have integrated it with kp 1.2, because a wider row gives a shallower steering slope, so a lower kp would soften steering too far. Do not expect a result from this race on the current candidate. Whether the wider row helps can be read from line-loss events after progress 0.1 on the s-bend and oval. Please also note that a 16 mm footprint may read more edge noise, so a rise in steering oscillation could be footprint size rather than reach.
requested_changes: Keep sensor_positions at x = ±0.03 (or ±0.03 in 0.015 m steps) at y = 0.04 with sensor_size 0.016 for the next race. If line loss still starts after progress 0.1 on the s-bend or oval, widen the reach further before moving the row forward: the row can extend to ±0.04 at 16 mm, which reaches about 0.06 m offset, so keep the outer sensor's footprint clear of the 0.06 m limit.

If slalom steering oscillation is still at or above 0.145 with the wider row, lower kp in the controller before narrowing the row, because the wider spacing already reduces steering slope. Do not move the row forward unless oscillation rises to 0.15 or more, since the Builder's own rule for a forward offset (y = 0.02) depends on that trigger.
If line loss begins near progress 0 rather than on bends, the coverage edge is not the cause, and the geometry should be held while start-up speed and entry gain are examined.
